subject: Television & Streaming
title: Game of Thrones and Fantasy on TV
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Game of Thrones and Fantasy on TV.

hook.text: Before Game of Thrones, nobody believed fantasy could work on television. Dragons and swords meant cheap and silly.

buildup.text: HBO spent $10 million per episode to make Westeros feel real. The production quality rivaled Hollywood blockbusters.

discovery.text: The show killed main characters without warning. Audiences learned that nobody was safe—and they couldn't stop watching.

twist.text: The final season divided fans so bitterly that the cultural conversation turned from love to rage almost overnight.

climax.text: Game of Thrones proved fantasy could dominate TV, but also that a bad ending can erase years of goodwill.

punchline.text: Eight years of brilliance undone by six episodes.

quiz.question: What storytelling technique made Game of Thrones feel uniquely suspenseful?
